stories.title: Shelton Shocks Alcaraz in 5-Set Marathon, Finishes at 3:30 AM ET (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: BEN SHELTON SHOCKS ALCARAZ. 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(10-6). Four hours 28 minutes. Finished at 3:30 AM ET. Shelton's first career win over Alcaraz sends him to the US Open semifinals.

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Shelton was 0-for-3 against Alcaraz. Last night he went the distance — and won. A 10-point match tiebreak, closed with an ace. New York stayed up until 3:30 AM ET for this one. Ben Shelton is going to his third Grand Slam semifinal.

facebook.long_form:
Nobody in New York went to bed early last night.

Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz went five sets at Arthur Ashe Stadium — 4 hours and 28 minutes of tennis that didn't end until approximately 3:30 AM ET, the latest finish in US Open history. When it was over, Shelton stood on court having just recorded the biggest win of his career: 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(10-6).

The final set came down to a 10-point match tiebreak, and Shelton closed it with an ace. That's fitting — he's made his living on power serves and crowd energy, and New York gave him everything it had.

Shelton was 0 for 3 against Alcaraz coming into the match. None of it mattered by the time the final point landed. He advances to his third Grand Slam semifinal, where he'll meet fellow American Frances Tiafoe.

Were you up watching? What did you think of the finish? 🎾
facebook.image_caption: The match finished at 3:30 AM ET. Score: 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(10-6). Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz for the first time in his career — on the biggest stage possible. The US Open keeps delivering.

stories.title: Tiafoe Completes Stunning Comeback Over Michelsen in 5 Sets (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: TIAFOE GOES THE DISTANCE. Down two sets, Frances Tiafoe rallied past Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6. The all-American US Open SF is set. One of them reaches the final.

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: He was two sets down. He won three straight. Frances Tiafoe is back in the US Open semifinals. On Friday he faces Ben Shelton. One of them is going to the US Open final. It will be an American.

facebook.long_form:
Frances Tiafoe has been here before — back against the wall, crowd on edge, needing to find something extra. Last night he found it again.

Down two sets to Alex Michelsen, Tiafoe turned the match completely around. Final score: 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6. Three sets in a row to close it out. It's the kind of performance that reminds you why Tiafoe is one of the most compelling players in the game — when the moment gets big, he tends to rise to meet it. 🎾

This is now Tiafoe's second US Open semifinal. On Friday, he'll face Ben Shelton in an all-American men's SF. One of them will play in the US Open final.

Who do you think wins — Tiafoe or Shelton?
facebook.image_caption: Down two sets. Won three straight. Frances Tiafoe is back in the US Open semifinals, and he's bringing the all-American energy with him.

stories.title: All-American Men's SF — Tiafoe vs. Shelton (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: For the first time in a generation, the US Open men's semifinals feature two Americans. Ben Shelton vs. Frances Tiafoe — Friday at Arthur Ashe. One of them is going to the US Open final.

facebook.long_form:
The US Open hasn't seen anything quite like this in a very long time.

Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe will meet in the men's semifinals on Friday — meaning a U.S. man is guaranteed to play in the final at Flushing Meadows. That's a big deal for American tennis, which has been waiting years for this kind of moment on the Grand Slam stage.

Shelton, 24, came to New York with a massive serve, an electric personality, and a knack for big-match tennis. Tiafoe, 26, came in as the experienced campaigner who knows how to handle the stage. These two are friends on the ATP Tour — and now they have to play for a spot in the US Open final.

Which American are you rooting for on Friday? 🇺🇸
facebook.image_caption: Shelton vs. Tiafoe. Friday. Arthur Ashe. Two Americans. One US Open final berth. This is what tennis fans in the States have been waiting for.

facebook.long_form:
The best women's match of the US Open is happening right now.

Coco Gauff — the 2023 US Open champion — takes on Mirra Andreeva — the 2026 French Open champion — at Arthur Ashe Stadium today, no earlier than 12:30 PM ET. Two of the best players in the world. Two major champions. And a rematch of this year's French Open SF, which Andreeva won. 🎾

Both players are 21 years old. Both have already won Grand Slams. The winner faces Aryna Sabalenka in the semifinals on Thursday — Sabalenka is going for her third consecutive US Open title. Whoever comes through today faces one of the toughest assignments in women's tennis.

Who wins — Gauff or Andreeva?

stories.title: Wednesday QF Day 2 — Zverev vs. Van de Zandschulp + Pegula vs. Navarro (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Wednesday evening at the US Open: Zverev vs. Van de Zandschulp at 6:30 PM ET. Then Pegula vs. Navarro — an all-American women's QF. An American woman is guaranteed in the semis from this side of the draw.

facebook.long_form:
Wednesday night at the US Open is still delivering. Two more quarterfinals go tonight.

In the men's draw, defending champion Alexander Zverev faces Botic van de Zandschulp at 6:30 PM ET at Arthur Ashe. Zverev won this title last year and has been one of the most consistent players in the tournament. Van de Zandschulp has been an underdog story throughout — and Zverev himself has acknowledged the Dutchman's affinity for this tournament.

In the women's draw, No. 3 Jessica Pegula takes on No. 26 Emma Navarro. Navarro beat Pegula at the 2024 US Open. She'll be looking to do it again. Either way, an American woman is guaranteed to be in the semifinals from this side of the bracket. 🎾

Which match are you most excited about tonight?
